column3: The Hebrew says “Sea of Reeds”; BSB uses the traditional “Red Sea.”
The Hebrew has “and” and “saying”; BSB adds the temporal introduction “At this time.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “sons of Esau”; BSB broadens this to “descendants.”
The Hebrew measures the land by the tread of a foot’s sole; BSB condenses this to “a footprint.”
Buying with silver is stated twice, with separate verbs for eating and drinking; BSB combines the clauses.
“Your hand” is singular in Hebrew, and the verb is “knew”; BSB has “hands” and interprets the knowledge as watching over the journey.
The Hebrew says “sons of Esau” and simply names the Arabah road from Elath and Ezion-geber; BSB adds “which comes up.”
The Hebrew first names “Moab” and refers to “his land”; BSB uses plural “Moabites” and “their land.” “Sons of Lot” becomes “descendants.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew uses “them” after the destruction verb, where BSB repeats “the Horites.” “Sons of Esau” becomes “descendants.”

The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses them to “said.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Sons of Ammon” is repeated twice in Hebrew, and “sons of Lot” is explicit; BSB uses “Ammonites” and “descendants.”
The Hebrew repeats “Rephaim”; BSB uses “who” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew says “from before them”; BSB explicitly supplies “the Ammonites.”
The Hebrew has “sons of Esau” and collective singular “the Horite”; BSB uses “descendants” and plural “Horites.”
The Hebrew makes the Caphtorites the active subject of destroying the Avvim; BSB uses a passive construction.
The Hebrew names the Arnon stream or wadi; BSB uses “Valley.”
The Hebrew says “upon the face of the peoples” and retains “all” before “heavens”; BSB omits those details.
The Hebrew says “words of peace”; BSB interprets this as “an offer of peace.”
The speaker uses singular “me” and “I” and repeats “on the road”; BSB uses plural “us” and “we” and supplies “main.”
The Hebrew uses singular “me,” “I,” and “my feet.” It separately says to sell food and give water; BSB uses plurals and combines both under “sell.”
The Hebrew has singular “me” and “I” and says “sons of Esau”; BSB uses plural “us” and “we” and “descendants.”
Close to the Hebrew.
